content.text: Drapers Jobs allows employers to list a variety of draping, design, merchandising, and retail roles at all career levels. Employers can access the job board's CV database of skilled local candidates.

Drapers Jobs has both standard and enhanced posting plans and a CV search tool. While the job board is a good option for local hiring, is is more expensive than competitors such as FashionJobs.com. The platform is also missing advanced hiring tools. Drapers Jobs allows employers to list a variety of draping, design, merchandising, and retail roles at all career levels. Employers can access the job board's CV database of skilled local candidates. The Premium plan pushes listings to the top of job search results every seven days on rotation for increased visibility. The job posting process is quick and easy. Employers can add their company logo to job posts for added brand awareness. The Top Job plan adds vacancies to the site's home page and pins them to the top of job search results for added reach. Unlike competitors, such as Fashion Workie, Drapers Jobs does not offer a free job posting plan.

Listings aren't promoted on the site's social media pages or distributed to other job portals. Drapers Jobs lacks applicant tracking and candidate matching services. We were unable to find any online reviews of Drapers Jobs. Drapers Jobs and FashionJobs.com both cater to the fashion industry, but the latter is the more affordable choice with free internship postings and a starting price of €149.00 for a standard post. By contrast, a single listing on Drapers Jobs costs £625.00 +VAT. Both sites offer featured listings, but only FashionJobs.com has a global reach. Like Drapers Jobs, Fashion Workie advertises fashion-related positions and offers employer branding. However, the former is slightly more feature-rich with access to a CV database of top-notch candidates. But while Drapers Jobs charges £625.00 +VAT per post, Fashion Workie has a free posting plan, making it the more affordable choice.

content.text: Founded in 2001 by Jean-Philippe Boudy, FashionJobs.com is a division of FashionNetwork.com. FashionJobs.com is the world's fastest growing job site for fashion, retail and luxury employment, with some 20,000 job offers uploaded each month.

News medias : FashionJobs.com has been named the best specialized employment website in France in a new classification by Les Echos, based on study of over 10,000 executives, human resources managers and headhunters.

The Paris daily, the French equivalent of the Financial Times, announced that FashionJobs.com – which specializes in careers in fashion retailing, communications, creation and management - topped the poll for a specialist job agency for 2017 in a study of over 10,000 different executives, human resources managers and headhunters. “The recruitment market in France is particularly atomized with some 3,500 agencies and 700 portals,” said Les Echos, which collaborated with Statista on this study. Les Echos ranked Linkedin as the leading generalist employment websites in the same study. While the esteemed financial newspaper stressed that in the specialized employment sector, “it is the expert FashionJobs.com which distinguishes itself.” · Les Echos also ranked Michael Page France as the leading management agency and Egon Zehnder as the top agency when seeking senior executives.

Founded in 2001 by Jean-Philippe Boudy, FashionJobs.com is a division of FashionNetwork.com. ## Why Fashion Workplace



A job board built specifically for the fashion industry, connecting professionals with
 brands across Europe.





### Built for fashion



Every listing on Fashion Workplace is a fashion role. No scrolling past unrelated industries to find what you are looking for.



### European focus



We cover roles across Europe, from London and Paris to Amsterdam, Copenhagen, Berlin, Milan, and beyond.



### Sustainable and ethical brands



We highlight employers with genuine sustainability commitments, including B-Corp certified companies, brands with published supplier lists, and businesses working toward circular models.



### Every function, every level



Whether you are a graduate looking for your first role or a senior leader making a move, we list positions across design, buying, marketing, sourcing, sustainability, operations, and more.



## The fashion industry in Europe



Europe is home to some of the world's most influential fashion markets, and the industry
 continues to evolve.



The European fashion industry employs millions of people across design, manufacturing,
 retail, logistics, and marketing. Major fashion capitals including Paris, Milan, London, and
 Copenhagen serve as headquarters for both established luxury houses and emerging independent
 brands. The industry spans everything from haute couture to high-street retail, with a
 growing segment of brands focused on sustainable and ethical practices.



Sustainability is reshaping the industry. EU legislation, including the Corporate
 Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products
 Regulation (ESPR), is creating new compliance requirements and driving demand for
 professionals with sustainability expertise. Circular business models, including rental,
 resale, and repair, are growing rapidly and creating new categories of roles that did not
 exist a decade ago.



At the same time, digital transformation is changing how fashion brands operate. E-commerce,
 data analytics, 3D design, and supply chain technology roles are increasingly common
 alongside traditional creative and commercial functions. For professionals with the right
 skills, the range of career paths in European fashion has never been broader.



## How it works



Finding your next fashion role is straightforward.





Step 1

Step 2



### Apply directly



Every listing links directly to the employer. Apply on their careers page with no intermediary and no hidden fees for job seekers.



Step 3



### Start your career



Join a fashion brand that matches your skills and values. Build a career in an industry you care about.

**Research notes:**

- **FashionUnited** (fashionunited.uk/fr/it/de/nl/be) dominates this space because it is genuinely the largest multi-country fashion-specific job network in Europe, with localised editions in each fashion-capital language. Each country edition lists distinct jobs, so they are separate sources for a digest.
- **BoF Careers** (businessoffashion.com/careers/jobs/europe/ — 1,249 listed European roles confirmed via Google) and **FashionJobs.com** (fr.fashionjobs.com/it.fashionjobs.com — confirmed highly active via Google snippets with LVMH/Guerlain/Chanel listings dated May 2026) were **not included** because direct web_fetch access was blocked (both return bot-check pages). They are strong real-world candidates and worth a manual check.
- **Drapers Jobs** dates (March 2026) are at the outer edge of the 60-day freshness window; the board has 2,500+ total listings and is continuously updated by the UK's most authoritative fashion trade title.
- **Fashion Workie** lacks visible post dates on the homepage but shows clearly active listings with named major brands and categorised role counts, suggesting a live board rather than a stale aggregator.
